ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a six-membered carbon ring, with a carbonyl C=O connected at the upper-right position of the ring, an R substituent below the ring, and a carbon chain extending to the right from the lower-right position of the ring; on the right side there is a C=C fragment and it is connected to a negatively charged oxygen atom. H–B is also drawn above, and there are multiple curved arrows in the figure. Reasoning: According to the draft method, first ignore all curved arrows, and exclude the H–B bond involving hydrogen. Count only bonds between non-hydrogen atoms: the six-membered ring on the left has 6 C–C bonds; the carbonyl C=O is 1 bond; the C–R substituent bond is 1 bond; in the chain extending to the right from the lower-right carbon of the ring there are 3 C–C single bonds; the C=C on the right is 1 bond; the C–O bond connected to the negatively charged oxygen is 1 bond. The total is 6 + 1 + 1 + 3 + 1 + 1 = 13.

method.method_draft: First ignore all curved arrows and the H–B bond because it involves hydrogen. Count the heavy-atom bonds by fragments: 6 C–C bonds around the left six-membered ring; 1 C=O bond to the upper oxygen; 1 C–R substituent bond; 3 C–C single bonds in the chain from the lower-right ring carbon toward the right; 1 right-side C=C double bond; and 1 C–O bond to the negatively charged oxygen. Add these fragment counts to obtain 13.
